decisions.reason: 말이 사무소지 빌딩이다 is the office-versus-building size joke; SOL’s “in name only” recasts it as a fake office.
“Making my way through” is the natural English for 거쳐; “working through” overstates labor.
“As if they were doing me a favor amounted to” is cleaner English for 적선하듯 / 날강도 수준 than stacked “like…were.”
SOL replaces 지역 with “branch” and adds “instead”; BASE keeps 찾은 곳이 이곳 and region.
“Unto itself” is a register bump for this narrator; “all by itself” matches 그 자체로 in his voice.
“Blatant discrimination” is the natural collocation for 대놓고 차별; “and asked” is cleaner than the participle.
“Endured” matches 겪었다; “shitty treatment” matches 더러운 꼴 without softening.
Need 그런 생각과 함께, which SOL drops, and 걸음을 뗀 순간이었다 as an interrupted “just started.”
decisions.replacement: I had just started walking with that thought when—

decisions.reason: Drops BASE’s misleading “just” for 다만 and places the footnote after the period.
가물가물하다 is hazy memory, not a full “couldn’t remember.”
저 당당함 뭔데 is “what’s with that confidence,” not a question about its source.
울려 퍼졌다 is “rang,” but SOL’s “quickly” is not in 붙었다가 떨어진다.
decisions.replacement: His hearty laugh rang through the hall. Nearly a hundred people looked over, then looked away.

decisions.reason: SOL adds “pretty” and weakens 마주치고 to “seen each other.”
옆에 있으면 is physical “next to me,” which “around” blurs.
“Knocked back in one gulp” is the idiomatic rendering of 한입에 털어 넣다.
Preserves 한두 번 counting; SOL flattens it and infers “ease.”
자식 is not specified as one child; 몸을 사리다 is “being more careful,” not “watching myself.”
decisions.replacement: “Not every day. I drop by now and then. Once I got married and had kids, I started being more careful. Heh heh.”

decisions.reason: 그게 뭐 대단한 일이라고 is a dismissive statement; the period keeps it from becoming a real question.
Preserves 대단한 건 대단한 거다 tautology; SOL flattens it to “it was a big deal.”
“First” keeps 살아 있어야 as a precondition; SOL drops it.
“Completed the ten years needed to qualify” is cleaner for 연금 지급 대상인 10년을 채우다.
Spoken English needs the subject “You” in that line.
“Seven years in” already matches 7년 찬데; SOL pads with “under my belt now.”
사무소 here is the manpower office, not generic offices.
Comma before “too” is a wash; no real gain.
The truncated “so Sopung Guild” matches the Korean fragment; SOL pads it.
자신만의 노하우 is “his own know-how,” not “plenty of.”
“My turn would only come after” is more natural word order for 후에야 내 차례가 돌아올.
“I’ll go on ahead” is the natural casual English for 먼저 갈게.
허허 웃었다 is an awkward/sheepish laugh, not a generic chuckle.
표정이 이상하더라니 is his expression looking off, not that he looked awkward.
못 본 사이 is time apart, matching the earlier “out of touch”; BASE’s “wasn’t looking” is the wrong idea.
“Ranking up on an F-rank’s potential” is translationese; SOL keeps 고작 한 단계 / 승급.
“See you around” is the natural goodbye for 또 보자.
네 and polite 봬요 are “Yes,” not casual “Yeah.”
작정한 듯 is determined pouring of names; SOL invents the speakers waiting for him to leave.
덤덤한 얼굴 is a blank face; “expression” is a needless synonym.
노려보았다 is glared; SOL weakens it to “looked.”
Subjectless 분배 후 is contract-speak; passive “are distributed according to contribution” matches that register.
게이트 등급 is a clipped period in the telegram exchange, not a marked question.
“Glared down his nose at me” is tighter English for 고압적인 시선으로 쏘아봤다.
“At the mention of” captures E급 게이트라는 말에; the rest stays the same plan.
트렁크 is the source loanword “trunk”; SOL genericizes it to “luggage compartment.”
있나 본데 needs “I guess”; 제가 형님이랑 keeps I-with-you, not SOL’s mutual “you and I.”
decisions.replacement: “Right? I guess I really do have a connection with you, hyung.”

decisions.reason: 얼굴이 부쩍 늙어 보였다 is his face looking older; SOL drops 얼굴.
아는 사이였다 is a fact, not “seemed to.”
Keeps 새로운 사람들 and 총 세 명; “Amid” is the wrong register.
SOL drops 어디 가서 from the rookie line.
고인물 파티 is the slangy two-word thought; “a party of old hands” flattens it.
낫다 is “better”; “more reliable” is an unsupported gloss.
젊은 친구는 is third-person-to-his-face, not the address “young man.”
첫 레이드부터 이런 식이면 곤란한데 is a first-raid problem, not “awkward before it started.”
입을 털었다 is ran his mouth; “hurried to explain” loses the idiom.
“Won’t be taking part in combat” matches 전투 참여는 일절 안 하고.
Blank-stare word order is a wash.
부연 설명 is extra/additional explanation, not “the whole explanation.”
됐어 is “drop it,” not the addressee-specific “leave him alone.”
오케이 했을 is “said yes/OK,” not the more formal “approved it.”
돌아가는 그림 is how this had gone, not generic “what had happened.”
Keeps the delayed beat 추천한 거다. 셔츠남, 최 팀장에게.
다 티 나 / 저 형님 is “all over him” and “that hyung,” not “your face” / “this hyung.”
“Why go through life hiding them” naturalizes 숨기고 살아 without changing the sense.
그럼 is “Right,” not the stronger “Exactly.”
수많은 is “many,” not “countless”; 순박 is guileless rather than BASE’s ambiguous “simple.”
decisions.replacement: I’d thought of Im Kkeokjeong as one of the many people I’d crossed paths with for a moment and moved on from. Meeting him again, he was more guileless and warmhearted than I’d expected.

decisions.reason: Keeps the 최 팀장, 최 팀장 repetition SOL flattens.
말했다 is spoke; SOL’s “looked back” is a different action.
고개를 돌리니 is turning his head, not merely “looked over.”
Slightly cleaner footnote grammar: article plus “bandit and folk hero.”
